opcodes.name: unreachable
opcodes.description:
The unreachable instruction causes an unconditional trap.

A trap immediately aborts execution. Traps cannot be handled by WebAssembly code, but are reported to the outside environment, where they typically can be caught.

The instructions after it are still validated, but against an unconstrained operand stack, so sequences that would not otherwise type-check are accepted there.

opcodes.name: nop
opcodes.description: The nop instruction does nothing.

opcodes.name: block
opcodes.description:
The beginning of a block construct, a sequence of instructions with a label at the end.

Both the parameter and result types come from the bt immediate.

The block, loop and if instructions are structured instructions. They bracket nested sequences of instructions, called blocks, terminated with, or separated by, end or else pseudo-instructions. They must be well-nested.

opcodes.name: loop

stack.note: Both the parameter and result types come from the bt immediate.

opcodes.description: A block with a label at the beginning which may be used to form loops.

opcodes.name: if

stack.note:
Both the parameter and result types come from the bt immediate.

The i32 on top is the condition: non-zero runs the first branch, zero runs the else-branch if there is one.

opcodes.description: The beginning of an if construct with an implicit then block.
opcodes.followedByNote: Then the instructions run when the condition is non-zero. Optionally 0x05 (else) and the instructions run when it is zero. Then 0x0B (end).

opcodes.name: else
opcodes.description:
Marks the else block of an if.

Not typed on its own: what it does to the stack belongs to the enclosing if.

opcodes.name: try
opcodes.description: Begins a block which can handle thrown exceptions.
opcodes.followedByNote: Then the instructions. Then zero or more 0x07 (catch) clauses, optionally ending with 0x19 (catch_all), or a single 0x18 (delegate). Then 0x0B (end).

stack.note: Both the parameter and result types come from the bt immediate.

opcodes.name: catch
opcodes.description:
Begins the catch block of the try block.

Not typed on its own: what it does to the stack belongs to the enclosing try.

opcodes.name: throw
opcodes.description: Creates an exception defined by the tag and then throws it.

stack.note: t* are the parameters of tag x.

opcodes.name: rethrow
opcodes.description: Pops the exnref on top of the stack and throws it.

opcodes.name: throw_ref
opcodes.description: Pops the exnref on top of the stack and throws it.

stack.note: Traps on a null exception reference.

opcodes.name: end
opcodes.description:
Marks the end of a block, loop, if, or function.

Not typed on its own: what it does to the stack belongs to the construct it closes.

opcodes.name: br
opcodes.description:
Branch to a given label in an enclosing construct.

Performs an unconditional branch.

A branch targeting a block or if behaves like a break statement in most C-like languages, while a branch targeting a loop behaves like a continue statement.
opcodes.followedByNote: Label 0 is the innermost structured instruction enclosing the branch; increasing indices refer to those further out.

opcodes.name: br_if
opcodes.description:
Performs a conditional branch, branching if i32 c is non-zero.

Conditionally branch to a given label in an enclosing construct.

opcodes.name: br_table
opcodes.description:
A jump table which jumps to a label in an enclosing construct.

Performs an indirect branch through an operand indexing into the label vector that is an immediate to the instruction, or to a default target if the operand is out of bounds.

opcodes.name: return
opcodes.description:
Return zero or more values from this function.

The return instruction is a shortcut for an unconditional branch to the outermost block, which implicitly is the body of the current function.

opcodes.name: call
opcodes.description: The call instruction invokes another function, consuming the necessary arguments from the stack and returning the result values of the call.

opcodes.name: call_indirect

stack.note: The i32 selects an entry of table x; the call traps unless that entry holds a function of type y. Before reference types this second immediate was always 0x00, the only table there was.

opcodes.description: The call_indirect instruction calls a function indirectly through an operand indexing into a table.

opcodes.name: return_call
opcodes.description:
The tail-call version of call.

The current frame is replaced instead of a new one being pushed, so a chain of tail calls runs in constant stack space.

stack.note: t* are the parameters of function x. The callee’s results become the current function’s, so execution does not continue past this instruction.

opcodes.name: return_call_indirect
opcodes.description:
The tail-call version of call_indirect.

The current frame is replaced instead of a new one being pushed, so a chain of tail calls runs in constant stack space.

stack.note: t* are the parameters of function type y, and the i32 indexes table x. The callee’s results become the current function’s, so execution does not continue past this instruction.

opcodes.name: call_ref
opcodes.description: Calls a function through a reference of type x.

stack.note: t1* and t2* are the parameters and results of function type x. Traps on a null reference.

opcodes.name: return_call_ref

stack.note: t* are the parameters of function type x. The callee’s results become the current function’s, so execution does not continue past this instruction. Traps on a null reference.

opcodes.description:
The tail-call version of call_ref.

The current frame is replaced instead of a new one being pushed, so a chain of tail calls runs in constant stack space.

opcodes.name: delegate
opcodes.description:
Begins the delegate block of the try block.

Not typed on its own: what it does to the stack belongs to the enclosing try.

opcodes.name: catch_all
opcodes.description:
Begins the catch_all block of the try block.

Not typed on its own: what it does to the stack belongs to the enclosing try.

opcodes.name: drop

stack.note: Works on any single value: t is whatever is on top.

opcodes.description:
The drop instruction simply throws away a single operand.

Arguably the only stack manipulation instruction WebAssembly has. There is no dup, swap or rot, and no way to reach past the top of the stack. See WebAssembly is not quite a stack machine, by purplesyringa.

opcodes.name: select

stack.note: Works on any value type, as long as both candidates have the same one, but only a number or vector type. For a reference, use the annotated form select t (0x1C).

opcodes.description: The select instruction selects one of its first two operands based on whether its third operand is zero or not.

opcodes.name: select t
opcodes.description: Only the annotated form can be used with reference types.

stack.note: t is given by the immediate rather than inferred, which is what lets this form take a reference.

opcodes.name: try_table
opcodes.description: Begins a block which can handle thrown exceptions.

stack.note: Both the parameter and result types come from the bt immediate.

opcodes.name: local.get
opcodes.description:
This instruction gets the value of a variable.

The index space for locals is only accessible inside a function and includes the parameters of that function, which precede the local variables.

The locals context refers to the list of locals declared in the current function (including parameters), represented by their value type.

opcodes.name: local.set
opcodes.description:
This instruction sets the value of a variable.

The index space for locals is only accessible inside a function and includes the parameters of that function, which precede the local variables.

opcodes.name: local.tee
opcodes.description:
The local.tee instruction is like local.set but also returns its argument.

The index space for locals is only accessible inside a function and includes the parameters of that function, which precede the local variables.

opcodes.name: global.get
opcodes.description:
This instruction gets the value of a variable.

The globals context is the list of globals declared in the current module, represented by their global type.

opcodes.name: global.set
opcodes.description: This instruction sets the value of a variable.

opcodes.name: table.get
opcodes.description:
Reads the element at a given index of table x.

Traps if the index is past the end of the table.

opcodes.name: table.set
opcodes.description:
Writes an element to a given index of table x.

Traps if the index is past the end of the table.

opcodes.name: i32.load

stack.note: The signatures on the memory instructions show a 32-bit memory. A 64-bit memory (memory64) takes and returns i64 addresses instead, including for memory.size and memory.grow.

opcodes.description:
Load 4 bytes as i32.

Memory is accessed with load and store instructions, which all take a memory immediate memarg holding an address offset and the expected alignment.

effective address = address operand + memarg.offset.

opcodes.name: i64.load
opcodes.description:
Load 8 bytes as i64.

The static offset is added to the address operand taken from the stack. For a 32-bit memory the sum is computed in 33 bits, so it cannot wrap; a 64-bit memory (memory64) takes an i64 address instead. All values are read and written in little endian byte order. A trap results if any accessed byte lies outside the memory’s current size.

opcodes.name: f32.load
opcodes.description:
Load 4 bytes as f32.

Note: When a number is stored into memory, it is converted into a sequence of bytes in little endian byte order.

opcodes.name: f64.load
opcodes.description: Load 8 bytes as f64.

opcodes.name: i32.load8_s
opcodes.description:
Load 1 byte and sign-extend i8 to i32.

Integer loads and stores can optionally specify a storage size that is smaller than the bit width of the respective value type. In the case of loads, a sign extension mode sx (s|u) is then required to select appropriate behavior.

opcodes.name: br_on_non_null
opcodes.description: Checks for null and branches if present.

stack.note: Branches to l if the reference is not null, carrying it to the label; otherwise leaves nothing.

opcodes.name: cont.new
opcodes.description: Part of the stack switching proposal, which adds continuations so a module can run several execution stacks — coroutines, generators, async/await and lightweight threads.

stack.note: ft is the function type that continuation type x wraps. Turns a function into a continuation that has not started running.

opcodes.name: cont.bind
opcodes.description: Part of the stack switching proposal, which adds continuations so a module can run several execution stacks — coroutines, generators, async/await and lightweight threads.

stack.note: Types: t* are arguments bound into the continuation ahead of time, which is why y takes fewer parameters than x. The specification writes them t3*.

opcodes.name: suspend
opcodes.description: Part of the stack switching proposal, which adds continuations so a module can run several execution stacks — coroutines, generators, async/await and lightweight threads.

stack.note: t1* and t2* are the parameters and results of tag x. Suspends to the nearest handler for that tag.

opcodes.name: resume
opcodes.description: Part of the stack switching proposal, which adds continuations so a module can run several execution stacks — coroutines, generators, async/await and lightweight threads.

stack.note: t1* and t2* are the parameters and results of continuation type x. The handler clauses say where control goes if the continuation suspends.

opcodes.name: resume_throw
opcodes.description: Part of the stack switching proposal, which adds continuations so a module can run several execution stacks — coroutines, generators, async/await and lightweight threads.

stack.note: Types: t* are the parameters of tag e, raised at the point where the continuation suspended. t2* are the results of continuation type x.

opcodes.name: resume_throw_ref
opcodes.description: Part of the stack switching proposal, which adds continuations so a module can run several execution stacks — coroutines, generators, async/await and lightweight threads.

stack.note: Takes an existing exception reference rather than a tag’s parameters, as throw_ref does beside throw. t2* are the results of continuation type x.

opcodes.name: switch
opcodes.description: Part of the stack switching proposal, which adds continuations so a module can run several execution stacks — coroutines, generators, async/await and lightweight threads.

stack.note: t1* and t2* are the parameters and results of continuation type x. Switches straight to another continuation rather than suspending to a handler.
